summary: We recommend shipping the citation-staleness downgrade as a single-point drop on citation_quality with a floor at 1 when a majority of citations have an accessed date older than STALE_CITATION_DAYS at the time of scoring because freshness is a leading indicator of un-reverified evidence without conflating it with correctness. The tradeoff against a harder ratchet that drops to 1 immediately is that a single-point downgrade preserves the rubric's existing 1-to-5 granularity and gives operators a visible warning before the gate hard-fails. The rule is implemented identically in sdk-python and sdk-typescript ported one-to-one and documented in specification appendix-a-rubric md with three new tests covering majority-stale fresh-no-downgrade and floor-at-1.

claims.statement: sdk-python open_outcome verifier py applies the staleness downgrade after computing the base citation_quality score and exports STALE_CITATION_DAYS as a module constant equal to 180 because the diff adds a datetime import a module-level constant and a post-score downgrade block that floors the result at 1.

claims.caveats: The 180 day threshold is conservative; D6 can pair this with an optional URL liveness check for stronger freshness signal.

claims.statement: sdk-typescript src verifier ts ports the same algorithm including the STALE_CITATION_DAYS constant and the floor-at-1 invariant because the TS diff restructures the score-and-justification block into mutable variables before applying the same majority-stale check using a UTC date subtraction.

claims.caveats: TS Date arithmetic uses setUTCDate to avoid local timezone drift; the python and TS implementations agree to within a wall-clock day.

open_questions: Should the staleness threshold be configurable per verifier instance rather than a module constant so different deployments can tune the freshness window without forking the SDK?
methodology_notes: Inspected the existing citation_quality scoring path in both SDKs then added the staleness downgrade in a single self-contained block per SDK with matching constants. Ran the full sdk-python test suite to confirm 27 of 27 pass including 3 new staleness tests.
